Buchach Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ternopilska oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Buchach was the birthplace of Shmuel Yosef Agnon (1888–1970), the first Hebrew-language writer to win the Nobel Prize in Literature (1966), as well as the Hebrew prose writer Yitzhak Pernhof (1865–1918). Jews were among the town's first settlers when it was founded in 1540, and by the mid-19th century supported 19 synagogues and a Hasidic dynasty founded by Avram David Warman, alongside many followers of the Chortkiv and Gusyatin Hasidic courts; a combined cholera epidemic and fire claimed 600 Jewish lives in 1881. The population peaked at 7,777 (54 percent of the town) by 1910. Between 1941 and 1943, the community was destroyed through repeated executions and deportations to the Bełżec death camp, with the ghetto's final liquidation in 1943 killing around 3,500 people; only about 500 local Jews survived the war.
